messages.content: Analyze this sentence.  "Consydre thou myne condicyon; reflecte upon myne fader. Shall I forsake hym, when he is strycken wyth blyndnesse and destytute, to wrastle wyth infirmitie and penurye, when it lyeth wythin my poure to rendre hys latter yeeres fylled wyth comforte and joye?" Each paragraph of your response must end with the same word it started with, separate paragraphs with a newline.

message.content:
Analysis This archaic sentence uses thou forms and a rhetorical question to plead against abandoning a suffering father Analysis
Translation Consider my condition; reflect upon my father; shall I forsake him when he is struck with blindness and destitute, to wrestle with infirmity and poverty, when it lies within my power to render his later years filled with comfort and joy Translation
Structure It opens with imperative clauses and continues with a complex interrogative sentence containing two when subordinate clauses Structure
Moral The moral appeal rests on the contrast between the suffering of the father and the power of the speaker to ease it Moral
Effect The effect is persuasive and emotionally charged Effect
